title: Adverbs
summary: Words that say how, where, when and how much: nang paupô, dáhan-dáhan, díto, saanmán, lagí, kung mínsan, kauntî…
goals: Make adverbs of manner with nang + pa- + verb root
Place an adverb of manner before or after the verb, with the right ligature
Use adverbs of place, such as sa + place, díto, saanmán and búhat sa … hanggáng
Use common adverbs of time and quantity

sections.title: Action words and how they are done

blocks.t: Some words show **actions**. Other words describe **how** the action was done. Those describing words are **adverbs**.

blocks.title: What an adverb does
blocks.t: An adverb **modifies an action word** (a verb). It tells **how**, **where** and **when** an action has happened, happens or will happen. This lesson also shows adverbs of **quantity** (how much).

blocks.title: Adverbs in English
blocks.t: In English the adverbs here are *high*, *down* and *loudly*. In the Tagalog examples, notice the little word **nang** in front of each describing word.

blocks.title: Four kinds of adverbs

blocks.t: An adverb of **manner** tells **how** an action occurred, occurs or will occur. Generally the article [[nang|other]] introduces it, and the adverb is made by attaching the prefix **pa-** to a verb root.

blocks.title: Like -ing words, but not quite
blocks.t: In English, **nang + pa- + verb root** comes out as an *-ing* word, like *sitting* and *standing*, which look like participles. But the book points out a difference: a pa- word in Tagalog **modifies verbs**, whereas an English participle modifies **nouns or pronouns**.

Adverbs also describe **where** an action took place, is taking place or will take place. All phrases with the preposition **sa** before the name of a place, specific or general, are adverbs of place.

blocks.title: Breaking up saanmán
blocks.t: **saanmán** is only broken up (**saán** … **man**) when the shortened pronoun **ka** (the singular *you*) is the subject. All other pronouns come **after** saanmán.

Tagalog has a considerable number of adverbs of **time**. Some are one-syllable words you met in Lesson 10 (like **na** and **pa**); others are phrases.

Because **sa** is such a versatile word (Lesson 26), it also makes adverbs of time when it is placed before **hours, days, months and years**: **sa Lunés** (*on Monday*), **sa hapon** (*in the afternoon*) and **sa Márso** (*in March*).

blocks.title: Remember
items: Adverbs tell how, where, when and how much an action happens.
Manner: nang + pa- + verb root (nang paupô). Ganitó, ganyán, ganoón; mabilís; dáhan-dáhan; biglâ, agâd.
Adverb before the verb: nang is lost and a ligature joins the words (Dáhan-dáhan siyang lumálákad; Dáhan-dáhan si Dulce na lumálákad).
Place: sa + place, díto / díyan / doón, saanmán (saán ka man), sa loób, sa labás, búhat sa … hanggáng.
Time: na, pa, nang / noóng, sandalî, pagkatapos, bágo, pirmí / paráti / lagí, tuwíng, saká na, kung mínsan, bihirá, samantála / habang, hábang-panahón.

exercises.q: What does an adverb do?
options: It tells how, where or when an action happens
It names a person or thing
It points to a person, like itó or iyán
exercises.answer: It tells how, where or when an action happens
exercises.explain: Adverbs modify action words.

exercises.q: Which word usually introduces an adverb of manner?
exercises.explain: nang + pa- + verb root: nang paupô.

exercises.q: Adverbs of manner such as paupô are made with which prefix?
exercises.explain: The prefix pa- is attached to a verb root: paupô, patayô, pahigâ.

exercises.q: "Ang batà ay nagbasá nang patayô" means…
exercises.explain: patayô = standing.

exercises.q: Which word means "like that" for something far from both speakers?
exercises.explain: ganitó (near the speaker), ganyán (near the one spoken to), ganoón (far from both).

exercises.q: Fill in: Dáhan-dáhan si Dulce ___ lumálákad.
exercises.explain: With a name as the subject, use the ligature na after it.

exercises.q: Fill in: Dáhan-dáhan ___ lumálákad. (She walks slowly.)
exercises.explain: With siya as the subject, use the ligature -ng: siyang.

exercises.q: What happens to nang when the adverb is placed BEFORE the verb?
options: It moves to the end of the sentence
exercises.explain: Lumálákad siya nang dáhan-dáhan → Dáhan-dáhan siyang lumálákad.

exercises.q: Which is another way to say "Siyá ay tumayó nang biglâ"?
exercises.explain: verb + ligature + adverb has the same meaning. With the adverb first, nang is lost.

exercises.q: Which phrase is an adverb of PLACE?
exercises.explain: Any sa + place phrase is an adverb of place.

exercises.q: When is saanmán broken up into saán … man?
exercises.explain: Saán ka man pumuntá, sásama ako.

exercises.q: "Kamí ay lumakad búhat sa baryo hanggáng sa lungsód" means…
options: We walked from the barrio to the city.
We will walk to the barrio.
exercises.answer: We walked from the barrio to the city.
exercises.explain: búhat sa … hanggáng = from … to.

exercises.q: What does noóng Lunés mean?
exercises.explain: noóng followed by a date also means last.

exercises.q: Which word means "every" (with -ng + a date)?
exercises.explain: Tuwíng Lúnes = every Monday.

exercises.q: pirmí, paráti and lagí all mean…
exercises.explain: Paráting nag-aáral si Peter. Peter always studies.

exercises.q: Kung mínsan, samantála and habang are used with which tense of verbs?
exercises.explain: Kung mínsan, nagagálit siyá. Sometimes she gets angry.

exercises.q: "Tayo ay matulog pagkatapos kumáin" means…
exercises.explain: pagkatapos (+ infinitive verb) = after.

exercises.q: Which word is the shortened form of kauntî (little)?
exercises.explain: Nagbigáy ng kontíng pagkain ang batàng maramot.

exercises.q: "Walâ akóng gustó" means…
exercises.explain: walâ = none; nothing.

recap: Adverbs describe how, where, when and how much an action happens.
Manner: nang + pa- + verb root (nagbasá nang paupô). Before the verb, nang is lost and a ligature joins: Dáhan-dáhan siyang lumálákad.
Place: sa + place (sa kusinà), díto / díyan / doón, saanmán, sa loób / sa labás, búhat sa … hanggáng.
Time: na, pa, noóng (last), sandalî, pagkatapos, bágo, lagí, tuwíng, saká na, kung mínsan, bihirá, samantála / habang, hábang-panahón.
